name: Left wing
summary: Left-wing politics, read as a positional label, is here the social-democratic and green parties that party-family datasets class on the left. They share equal rights, universal public services, unions and wage floors, climate action and international cooperation; they split on nuclear power and weapons and on growth.
scope: Positional-label family entry. Branches are the party families that ParlGov and the Chapel Hill Expert Survey code separately from one another (Social democracy / Socialist, and Green). The radical or far left (communist, revolutionary socialist, anarchist), which March and the CHES coding set apart as a distinct family and challenger to social democracy, is left out and has its own entry (far-left politics), as do centre-left politics, social democracy and green politics as single subjects. A position counts only where several of the listed branches state it and none the opposite; opposite positions are 0, low; silence is null.
